learn.rule: An outline turns notes into a plan: one topic sentence, three supporting details, and a concluding point. Then each part becomes a sentence.
learn.ruleEs: Un esquema convierte las notas en un plan: una oración temática, tres detalles de apoyo y una conclusión. Luego cada parte se convierte en una oración.
learn.model: Topic sentence: Bees are essential to the food we eat. Detail 1: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
learn.notice: The topic sentence is the big idea. Each detail adds one specific fact that supports it.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence best organizes these notes about bees?
items.text: Notes: bees carry pollen from flower to flower; apples, almonds, and blueberries depend on pollination; farmers move hives into orchards in spring.

options.text: Bees make honey in hives, which are often kept by beekeepers.
Apples are a popular fruit that people eat fresh or bake in pies.
This outline is about bees.
Bees are essential to the food people grow.

items.why: The topic sentence has to cover all the notes. Essential to food covers pollen, crops, and hives, while the other choices cover only one note or announce a topic.
items.whyEs: La oración temática debe cubrir todas las notas. Esencial para la comida cubre el polen, los cultivos y las colmenas; las otras opciones cubren solo una nota o anuncian un tema.

items.prompt: Check the notes that belong under the topic sentence 'Bees are essential to the food we eat.'

options.text: Bees carry pollen from one flower to another.
Some bees can sting when they feel threatened.
Almond and apple trees need pollination to produce fruit.
Wasps build nests out of paper.
Farmers bring hives into orchards during blooming season.

items.why: Details under this topic sentence must connect to food. Stinging and wasp nests are true facts, but they do not explain how bees support food.
items.whyEs: Los detalles de esta oración temática deben relacionarse con la comida. Las picaduras y los nidos de avispas son datos ciertos, pero no explican cómo las abejas ayudan a producir alimentos.

items.prompt: Complete the second detail in the bee outline.
parts: almonds and blueberries, depend on pollination.
items.model: Detail 2: Many fruits and nuts, such as almonds and blueberries, depend on pollination.
items.why: Such as introduces examples, and the commas set the examples apart. The other choices change the meaning.
items.whyEs: Such as introduce ejemplos, y las comas los separan. Las otras opciones cambian el significado.

items.prompt: Put the parts of the bee outline in order.
lines: Topic sentence: Bees are essential to the food we eat.
Detail 1: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
Detail 2: Many fruits and nuts cannot grow without pollination.
Detail 3: Farmers bring hives to orchards when the trees bloom.
Concluding point: Protecting bees helps protect our food supply.
items.why: An outline starts with the topic sentence, lists the details in order, and ends with the concluding point.
items.whyEs: Un esquema empieza con la oración temática, enumera los detalles en orden y termina con la conclusión.

items.prompt: Which concluding point best finishes the bee outline?
items.text: Outline so far: Bees are essential to the food we eat. They carry pollen. Many crops depend on pollination. Farmers bring hives to orchards.

options.text: Protecting bees means protecting the food that reaches our tables.
Bees are insects that live in large colonies around the world.
Honey tastes sweet on warm toast in the morning.
Next, I will write about butterflies.

items.why: A concluding point links back to the topic sentence and says why it matters. The other choices add a fact, an opinion, or a new topic.
items.whyEs: Una conclusión se conecta con la oración temática y dice por qué importa. Las otras opciones agregan un dato, una opinión o un tema nuevo.

write.prompt: Write a paragraph from the outline. Turn each part into a sentence and connect them with signal words.
write.promptEs: Escribe un párrafo a partir del esquema. Convierte cada parte en una oración y conéctalas con palabras de señal.
write.text: Topic sentence: Bees are essential to the food we eat. Detail 1: They carry pollen from flower to flower. Detail 2: Many crops cannot grow without pollination. Detail 3: Farmers bring hives into orchards. Concluding point: Protecting bees protects our food.

write.model: Bees are essential to the food we eat. First, they carry pollen from flower to flower, which allows plants to make seeds and fruit. Second, many crops, such as almonds and blueberries, cannot grow without this pollination. Third, farmers bring hives into orchards when the trees bloom. In conclusion, protecting bees helps protect our food supply.

familyTalk.en: Pick a food you eat this week and outline one big idea about it with three details. Say it aloud as a paragraph.
familyTalk.es: Elijan un alimento que coman esta semana y hagan un esquema con una idea principal y tres detalles. Dígalo en voz alta como un párrafo.

teacherTip.en: Have students cover the outline after reading it once and say the paragraph from memory with the signal words.
teacherTip.es: Pide que tapen el esquema después de leerlo una vez y que digan el párrafo de memoria con las palabras de señal.

learn.rule: An outline turns notes into a plan: one topic sentence, three supporting details, and a concluding point. Then each part becomes a sentence.
learn.ruleEs: Un esquema convierte las notas en un plan: una oración temática, tres detalles de apoyo y una conclusión. Luego cada parte se convierte en una oración.
learn.model: Topic sentence: Unit rates help shoppers compare prices fairly. Detail 1: A unit rate shows the cost of one unit, such as one ounce.
learn.notice: A math paragraph still has a big idea, and each detail uses a number or an example.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence should lead the unit-rate outline?
items.text: Notes: a unit rate gives the cost of one unit; a 12-ounce jar costs $3.00; a 20-ounce jar costs $4.40; the smaller price per ounce is the better buy.

options.text: A 12-ounce jar costs $3.00 at the store.
Unit rates help shoppers compare prices fairly.
Division is an operation that splits a number into equal parts.
I will explain math.

items.why: The topic sentence names the big idea that the number notes support. The other choices are one fact, a vague statement, or an announcement.
items.whyEs: La oración temática nombra la idea principal que apoyan las notas con números. Las otras opciones son un solo dato, algo vago o un anuncio.

items.prompt: Check the notes that are strong supporting details for the unit-rate paragraph.

options.text: Many stores have a produce section.
A unit rate tells the cost of one unit, such as one ounce.
A 12-ounce jar for $3.00 costs $0.25 per ounce.
Jars can be made of glass or plastic.
A 20-ounce jar for $4.40 costs $0.22 per ounce, so it is the better buy.

items.why: Strong details explain or show the big idea with numbers. Facts about produce sections and jar materials do not help compare prices.
items.whyEs: Los detalles fuertes explican o muestran la idea principal con números. Los datos sobre secciones de la tienda y materiales de los frascos no ayudan a comparar precios.

items.prompt: Finish the number details by choosing the correct values.
parts: Detail 2: A 12-ounce jar costs $3.00, so its unit rate is
per ounce. Detail 3: A 20-ounce jar costs $4.40, so its unit rate is $0.22 per ounce, which is
items.model: Detail 2: A 12-ounce jar costs $3.00, so its unit rate is $0.25 per ounce. Detail 3: A 20-ounce jar costs $4.40, so its unit rate is $0.22 per ounce, which is less than the first jar's rate.
items.why: Divide $3.00 by 12 to get $0.25. Since $0.22 is smaller than $0.25, the larger jar costs less per ounce.
items.whyEs: Divide $3.00 entre 12 para obtener $0.25. Como $0.22 es menor que $0.25, el frasco grande cuesta menos por onza.

items.prompt: Put the parts of the unit-rate outline in order.
lines: Topic sentence: Unit rates help shoppers compare prices fairly.
Detail 1: A unit rate shows the cost of one unit, such as one ounce.
Detail 2: A 12-ounce jar for $3.00 costs $0.25 per ounce.
Detail 3: A 20-ounce jar for $4.40 costs $0.22 per ounce, so it is the better buy.
Concluding point: Unit rates make fair comparisons possible when package sizes differ.
items.why: The topic sentence leads, the details move from the definition to the examples, and the concluding point returns to fairness.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero, los detalles pasan de la definición a los ejemplos y la conclusión vuelve a la idea de comparar con justicia.

items.prompt: Which concluding point matches the unit-rate outline?
items.text: Outline so far: Unit rates help shoppers compare prices fairly. A unit rate gives the cost of one unit. One jar costs $0.25 per ounce and the other costs $0.22 per ounce.

options.text: Shoppers like to buy jars because they are easy to store at home.
Math class is held every day, and students bring calculators.
In conclusion, unit rates let shoppers compare prices fairly, even when package sizes are different.
Next, I will explain how to add fractions.

items.why: A concluding point connects back to the topic sentence. The other choices are off topic or begin a new one.
items.whyEs: Una conclusión se conecta con la oración temática. Las otras opciones se salen del tema o empiezan uno nuevo.

write.prompt: Write a paragraph from the outline. Use each part, include the numbers, and add signal words.
write.promptEs: Escribe un párrafo a partir del esquema. Usa cada parte, incluye los números y agrega palabras de señal.
write.text: Topic sentence: Unit rates help shoppers compare prices fairly. Detail 1: A unit rate shows the cost of one unit. Detail 2: A 12-ounce jar for $3.00 costs $0.25 per ounce. Detail 3: A 20-ounce jar for $4.40 costs $0.22 per ounce. Concluding point: Unit rates make comparisons fair.

write.model: Unit rates help shoppers compare prices fairly. First, a unit rate shows the cost of one unit, such as one ounce. For example, a 12-ounce jar that costs $3.00 has a unit rate of $0.25 per ounce. In addition, a 20-ounce jar that costs $4.40 has a unit rate of $0.22 per ounce, so it is the better buy. In conclusion, unit rates make fair comparisons possible when package sizes are different.

familyTalk.en: Next time you shop together, compare two sizes of the same food. Say the price per unit and which is the better buy.
familyTalk.es: La próxima vez que compren juntos, comparen dos tamaños del mismo alimento. Digan el precio por unidad y cuál conviene más.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to circle the numbers in the outline and tell where each belongs in their paragraph.
teacherTip.es: Pide que encierren en un círculo los números del esquema y que digan dónde va cada uno en su párrafo.

sets.title: The Industrial Revolution Outline
sets.titleEs: El esquema de la Revolución Industrial

learn.rule: An outline turns notes into a plan: one topic sentence, three supporting details, and a concluding point. Then each part becomes a sentence.
learn.ruleEs: Un esquema convierte las notas en un plan: una oración temática, tres detalles de apoyo y una conclusión. Luego cada parte se convierte en una oración.
learn.model: Topic sentence: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived. Detail 1: Steam-powered machines let factories make goods faster than hand workers.
learn.notice: The topic sentence is broad, and each detail is one specific change.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence best organizes these Industrial Revolution notes?
items.text: Notes: steam engines powered new machines; families moved from farms to crowded cities; factory workers faced long hours and unsafe conditions.

options.text: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived.
Steam engines burn coal to heat water and make steam.
Many people lived in cities during the nineteenth century.
I am going to explain the Industrial Revolution.

items.why: The topic sentence covers machines, moving to cities, and working conditions. The other choices are one narrow note or an announcement.
items.whyEs: La oración temática cubre las máquinas, la mudanza a las ciudades y las condiciones de trabajo. Las otras opciones son una sola nota o un anuncio.

items.prompt: Check the three notes that should be supporting details, not the topic sentence.

options.text: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived.
Machines such as the steam engine let factories make goods faster than hand workers.
Many families moved from farms to crowded cities to find factory jobs.
Long hours and unsafe conditions led reformers to demand new labor laws.
Roman engineers built aqueducts to carry water.

items.why: The first note is the big idea, so it belongs in the topic sentence. The Roman aqueducts are a different time and topic.
items.whyEs: La primera nota es la idea principal, así que va en la oración temática. Los acueductos romanos son de otra época y otro tema.

items.prompt: Complete two detail sentences with the best connecting words.
parts: Many families moved from farms to cities
factories offered paid jobs. Factories could make goods quickly,
items.model: Many families moved from farms to cities because factories offered paid jobs. Factories could make goods quickly, so the price of cloth dropped.
items.why: Because gives the reason families moved. So shows the result of faster production: cloth became cheaper.
items.whyEs: Because da la razón por la que las familias se mudaron. So muestra el resultado de producir más rápido: la tela se volvió más barata.

items.prompt: Put the parts of the Industrial Revolution outline in order.
lines: Topic sentence: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived.
Detail 1: Machines such as the steam engine let factories make goods faster.
Detail 2: Many families moved from farms to crowded cities because factories offered jobs.
Detail 3: Long hours and unsafe conditions led reformers to demand new labor laws.
Concluding point: These changes helped shape the modern world of work.
items.why: The outline moves from the big idea to three details and ends with a point about the lasting effect.
items.whyEs: El esquema va de la idea principal a tres detalles y termina con un punto sobre el efecto duradero.

items.prompt: Which concluding point best finishes the Industrial Revolution outline?
items.text: Outline so far: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived. Machines sped up production. Families moved to cities. Reformers demanded labor laws.

options.text: Factories are large buildings where many machines are kept.
The next topic in our unit is ancient Greece and its city-states.
In conclusion, the changes of the Industrial Revolution still shape how people work today.
Cloth is made from cotton or wool, and it can be dyed many colors.

items.why: A concluding point connects the details to why the topic matters now. The other choices are facts or a new topic.
items.whyEs: Una conclusión conecta los detalles con la razón por la que el tema importa hoy. Las otras opciones son datos o un tema nuevo.

write.prompt: Write a paragraph from the outline. Use each part and add signal words so the ideas connect.
write.promptEs: Escribe un párrafo a partir del esquema. Usa cada parte y agrega palabras de señal para conectar las ideas.
write.text: Topic sentence: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived. Detail 1: Machines let factories make goods faster. Detail 2: Families moved from farms to cities for factory jobs. Detail 3: Unsafe conditions led reformers to demand labor laws. Concluding point: These changes shaped the modern world of work.

label: I wrote at least 30 words
Escribí al menos 30 palabras
I used signal words such as first, second, or in conclusion
Usé palabras de señal como first, second o in conclusion
I used key words from the outline
Usé palabras clave del esquema
My last sentence ends with a period

write.model: The Industrial Revolution changed how people worked and lived. First, machines such as the steam engine let factories make goods faster than workers using hand tools. Second, many families moved from farms to crowded cities because factories offered jobs. Finally, long hours and unsafe conditions led reformers to demand new labor laws. In conclusion, these changes helped shape the modern world of work.

familyTalk.en: Ask a family member how work has changed since they were young. Outline one big idea and three changes together.
familyTalk.es: Pregunten a un familiar cómo ha cambiado el trabajo desde que era joven. Hagan juntos un esquema con una idea principal y tres cambios.

teacherTip.en: Model turning one outline line into a full sentence, then let pairs convert the rest.
teacherTip.es: Muestra cómo convertir una línea del esquema en una oración y luego deja que las parejas conviertan el resto.
